name: r134a_condenser_heat_rejection
title: R134a heat-pump condenser heat rejection and COP (Cengel 6-54)
summary: R134a enters a heat-pump condenser at 800 kPa and 35 °C at 0.018 kg/s and leaves at 800 kPa as saturated liquid. The heat rejection and the heat-pump COP follow from the open-system energy balance and a power input of 1.2 kW. Textbook exercise Cengel 6-54.

verification.summary: Against the stored solution of 06-54.EES: 10 common variables, 2 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 8. Maximum relative difference 6.08e-01 on h_out. The two are absolute h_in and h_out (R134a reference state). Q_dot_h is 3163.02 W against 3163.52 W; COP is 2.63585 against 2.63626.
verification.reference: EES stored solution in 06-54.EES (10 variables, EES X9.920)
verification.notes: 10 common variables, 2 differ above rtol=0.001: h_in 3.53e-01, h_out 6.08e-01 (compare_solution.py). Maximum over all common variables is 6.08e-01. Enthalpy offsets are +148146.609 J/kg (h_in) and +148174.032 J/kg (h_out). Saturated liquid R134a at -40 C in this binary is h = 148144.046 J/kg, s = 795.610 J/kg-K (EES refrigerant reference h = s = 0). EES stored no entropy. The two enthalpy offsets differ by 27.423 J/kg, which is the whole gap on the condenser enthalpy drop (175723.49 J/kg vs 175750.91 J/kg, relative 1.56e-04, below rtol). --all: Q_dot_h and COP 1.56e-04, M_dot p_in p_out T_in W_dot_in x_out 0. The 8 CoolSolve-only names are the diagram arrays P[i], h[i], T[i], s[i]. 0 iterations with and without .initials. The diagram block does not change the 10 original variables.
